newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ MP Morgan admits sought cash for interview.
newsitem.headline: NZ MP Morgan admits sought cash for interview.

text.p: New Zealand government MP Tukoroirangi Morgan acknowledged on Thursday he sought payment for a television interview in a move that has enraged politicians.

Two television stations said on Wednesday evening they had been approached by a lawyer claiming to represent Morgan, who is in the middle of two libel actions, offering to sell them his story for more than NZ$20,000 ($14,000).
The MP is a member of New Zealand First, the junior partner in New Zealand's centre-right coalition government which has a one-seat majority in the 120-member parliament.
Morgan had denied the claim in Wellington on Wednesday, saying the Auckland lawyer, Chris Reid, was not acting on his instructions.

Morgan is currently involved in pursuing one libel action, against opposition Labour Party MP Trevor Mallard and certain news media, and defending himself against a defamation suit from a Maori tribal trust.
Earlier on Wednesday evening TV3 played a taped conversation with Reid in which he said Morgan was going to have difficulties with finances so was looking for an offer.
"If you are prepared to pay for an interview, he'd give it to you exclusively," Reid told a TV3 news reporter.

Morgan's initial denial was backed up by his party leader and Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters on Wednesday night, but on Thursday Morgan issued a statement admitting he instructed contacts to be made.

"Through my barrister Peter Williams QC I gave instructions that Chris Reid be engaged to enter into negotiations of a confidental nature with the news media...", Morgan said in a statement issued through Reid.
A spokesman for Peters's office said no comment was available as yet from the party leader, who was travelling.

Morgan and Williams sought to explain the MP's change of heart over the issue by saying that there were telephone problems between Morgan and Reid during Wednesday afternoon when they were in different cities.

Morgan's political career has been marred by his involvement with publicly-funded pilot Maori language broadcaster Aotearoa Television Network (ATN) which is being investigated the Serious Fraud Office.
MPs from several parties accused Morgan of resorting to chequebook journalism, telling Radio New Zealand it was unheard of in their parliament.
Morgan has been heavily criticised in recent months for refusing media interviews on the ATN affair and ducking questions in parliament, claiming the matter was sub judice.
